cues: The thylakoid membranes hold the pigments.
Chlorophyll a is the only one that can turn light into chemical energy: it is the reaction-centre pigment.
Chlorophyll b, carotenes and xanthophylls are accessory pigments.
They catch other colours and pass the energy on, and carotenoids also protect chlorophyll from damage by too much light.
text: The thylakoid membranes hold the pigments. Chlorophyll a is the only one that can turn light into chemical energy: it is the reaction-centre pigment. Chlorophyll b, carotenes and xanthophylls are accessory pigments. They catch other colours and pass the energy on, and carotenoids also protect chlorophyll from damage by too much light.
